correctness.rationale: For any embedding fix source-period spans v_j of each chosen letter. The period-span inequality sum(v_j-1)+descents<=k-1 follows from monotone source positions; weighted length <=sum selected a_i + M sum(v_j-1)<=P+(k-1)M. Equality forces all q symbols, no index descents, full physical run inclusion, and extra periods only on maximum-weight letters. Each weak composition t_i of k-1 across r maximizing weights constructs a distinct valid subsequence; count binom(k+r-2,r-1). Checks enumerate entire distinct subsequence languages for 72 bounded weighted templates and k<=3, matching exact maxima and optimal output strings. Unrestricted classification follows from the span argument.

value.rationale: Repeated distinct-letter block templates are a natural tractable restricted family of an NP-hard genomic string problem. The period-span invariant yields not only a sharp length formula but all optimizer strings and degeneracy as a binomial coefficient, useful for exact benchmarking and tie counts. This is a motivated complete structural classification rather than a one-off tiny instance.
